text:
jordan: Customer reports a 403 on /v1/generate after a key rotation. They included a request id `r-7f3b2a` and a curl they used. Says it worked yesterday, failing today.

jordan: ```bash
curl -X POST https://api.redwood.ai/v1/generate \
  -H "Authorization: Bearer sk_live_OLD" \
  -H "Redwood-Org: org-abc" \
  -d '{"model":"redwood-1","input":"hi"}'
```

jordan: Response was HTTP 403 with this body:

jordan: ```json
{ "error": "forbidden", "message": "org scope mismatch", "request_id": "r-7f3b2a" }
```

mira: ACK. Quick checks: which key (org-scoped vs project-scoped) are they using? Often a project-scoped key against an org-scoped resource yields this. Can you ask them for the exact `Authorization` header and the `Redwood-*` header they set?

alex: I tried to repro in staging with a rotated key we have flagged as project-scoped. Running their curl (adjusted) returned `invalid_scope`.

alex: ```bash
curl -i -X POST https://api.redwood.ai/v1/generate \
  -H "Authorization: Bearer sk_rotated_example" \
  -H "Redwood-Project: proj-xyz" \
  -d '{"model":"redwood-1","input":"test"}'
```

alex: ```http
HTTP/1.1 403 Forbidden
Content-Type: application/json
X-Request-ID: r-9c1d55
{
  "error":"access_denied",
  "message":"token does not have access to org org-abc",
  "request_id":"r-9c1d55"
}
```

mira: Looks like a project-scoped token was used while the target resource expected an org scope. Ask the customer to either switch the header to `Redwood-Project: proj-xyz` (if they intended project access) or generate an org-scoped key and use that. Provide both curl examples as repro.

jordan: I'll request: (1) full `Authorization` header (they can mask middle chars), (2) exact `Redwood-*` header they sent, (3) support:collect_debug_bundle output or run `support:collect_debug_bundle --request-ids r-7f3b2a` and attach.

alex: Pulled server logs for similar request id r-9c1d55: auth subsystem shows `token_scope=project:proj-xyz, target_scope=org:org-abc -> reject`.

mira: That matches. Likely root cause = key scope mismatch after rotation. Also ask billing/security if the rotation created temporary scoped tokens.

jordan: @debug-bot could you create a debug bundle for org `org-abc` including request IDs [r-7f3b2a, r-9c1d55]?

debug-bot: Created debug bundle bundle-2026-03-17-001. URL: https://redwood-internal/bundles/bundle-2026-03-17-001 (access limited to support + eng-runtime).

mira: I'll review the bundle; if the token mapping looks off I'll ping eng-runtime. For a customer-facing quick fix, advise them to: generate a new org-scoped key in console -> replace Authorization header -> retry.

jordan: I'll reply to the customer with both curl examples, the sample server log snippet, and the bundle link. Marking this as P2 escalation. :thumbsup:

alex: Note added in ticket: repro verified in staging, root cause = token scope mismatch. Will reopen if bundle shows anything else.

mira: Sounds good. Will close thread once customer confirms the retry fixed it.
